subject: Nanotechnology
title: DNA Robots
description: A short lesson to help you apply DNA Robots.

hook.text: A DNA robot sorts molecular cargo on a surface — picking up fluorescent particles and placing them in the right bin.

buildup.text: The robot is a single-stranded DNA with a leg domain, a foot, and an arm — it walks randomly until it finds cargo.

discovery.text: When the arm encounters matching cargo, it picks it up — then random walking continues until a drop-off site is reached.

twist.text: The sorting takes 24 hours for 6 molecules — incredibly slow, but it proves algorithmic molecular behavior works.

climax.text: Lulu Qian's lab at Caltech demonstrated this in 2017 — the first cargo-sorting DNA nanorobot, published in Science.

punchline.text: A DNA robot that sorts molecules — slow, but a genuine nanoscale automaton.

quiz.question: How does the DNA cargo-sorting robot find and deliver its payload?
options: It is guided by a magnetic field to the correct location
It walks randomly until encountering cargo, picks it up, then walks until finding the correct drop-off site
A laser beam steers the robot to each cargo location sequentially
